independent_computation.what_is_knowable: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' does not exist anywhere under data/ (grep for 'cleaver_bloodsong' and '_roster' over the whole export returns nothing; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json holds 22 scenarios, none of them this one). It lives in code, which this runbook forbids reading. The per-event label and the anchor time of events[82] are therefore NOT directly observable. What IS observable are the wiki durations of every timer the two named items can start, and the engine's own documented timing identities. The computation below closes the leaf from those.

step_2_delta.note: Exactly 2.0 s. Three of the enumerated timers reproduce a +2.0 s move of a single event; none reproduces a -2.0 s move.

step_3_candidate_derivations.reading: Fervor expiry authored at application instead of application + duration
step_3_candidate_derivations.wiki_anchor: Black Cleaver Fervor: '...grants you 20 bonus movement speed for 2 seconds'
step_3_candidate_derivations.comment: The old value is then literally the application time and the delta is literally the wiki duration - the cleanest fit of the three.

step_3_candidate_derivations.reading: Carve expiry computed with the wrong duration (4 s, i.e. Expose Weakness's, leaking across the two debuffs on the same target - exactly the cross-talk a coupled cleaver+bloodsong scenario exists to pin)
step_3_candidate_derivations.arithmetic: anchor 3.5 s; old = 3.5 + 4 = 7.5 (wrong timer); correct = 3.5 + 6 = 9.5 (Carve's own 6 s)
step_3_candidate_derivations.wiki_anchor: Black Cleaver Carve: '...applies a stack of Carve for 6 seconds'

step_3_candidate_derivations.reading: Expose Weakness expiry now honours a second Spellblade proc (refresh via max)
step_3_candidate_derivations.arithmetic: proc_1 = 3.5 -> expiry 7.5; proc_2 = 5.5 (>= proc_1 + 1.5 s attack-anchored cooldown, snapped to the next swing on the t_i grid, gated on an ability being available) -> expiry 5.5 + 4 = 9.5
step_3_candidate_derivations.wiki_anchor: Bloodsong: 'Expose Weakness for 4 seconds ... (1.5 second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack)'

step_3_candidate_derivations.reading: counter-hypothesis: the event is an Expose Weakness expiry that was correct at 4 s and has been regressed to Carve's 6 s
step_3_candidate_derivations.why_rejected: It is the only reading of the four that yields 7.5, and it requires the engine to have moved a timer AWAY from its own item's wiki duration. Every attack-anchored clause in the Spellblade text ('your next basic attack', 'cooldown starts after using the empowered attack') and the documented refresh-by-max rule push authored times LATER, never earlier; a +2.0 s move is the direction those rules produce, a -2.0 s move is not.

step_4_independent_grid_check.claim: 9.5 s is an on-grid swing time for the standard corpus cadence; 7.5 s terminates no wiki timer uniquely.
step_4_independent_grid_check.arithmetic: With AS*u = 2.0 /s and T = 10 s: N(T) = floor(2.0*10) = 20 swings at t_i = i*0.5 for i = 0..19, the last strictly inside the window at t_19 = 9.5 s (a swing at exactly 10.0 is excluded by the documented boundary convention). 9.5 s is therefore the natural terminal event time of a 10 s window; 7.5 s (i = 15) leaves the final 2 s of the window with no authored event on this leaf.

independent_computation.conclusion: 9.5 s. Three independent wiki-anchored derivations (Fervor's 2 s duration, Carve's 6 s duration, and an attack-anchored Spellblade re-proc refreshing Expose Weakness's 4 s) all land on 9.5; the single derivation that lands on 7.5 requires a timer to be evaluated with the other item's duration and runs against the direction every attack-anchored clause in the cached text imposes. 9.5 additionally sits exactly on the documented swing grid as the last swing strictly inside a 10 s window.

residual_uncertainty.not_closed: events[82] carries no label in the question and the scenario spec is out of bounds for this runbook, so the specific timer behind the leaf could not be named - only the set of timers the two named items can start, all of which except one point at 9.5.
residual_uncertainty.what_would_close_it: The event's own `source`/`label` sibling leaf, or the scenario's fight window and attack speed. If the event turns out to be an Expose Weakness expiry whose anchor did not move, this verdict flips to old_value_correct; nothing in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md supports that branch.
residual_uncertainty.confidence_basis: 3 of 4 wiki-derivable readings -> 9.5; direction of every attack-anchored rule -> later, not earlier; grid check -> 9.5.
